strategy_definition.summary: Fair value gaps, balanced price ranges, liquidity voids, and volume imbalances act as points of interest where price rebalances inefficient price delivery. These imbalances offer the strongest trading opportunities when overlapping with another previously established PD array.

timeframes.notes: Fractal across all timeframes. High-impact news events (FOMC, CPI, NFP) leave liquidity voids on lower timeframes, while volume imbalances and voids are also demonstrated on daily and futures charts.

other: Imbalance should preferably overlap with another PD array (such as an order block, breaker block, or mitigation block)

glossary.BISI: Buy-side imbalance, sell-side inefficiency; functionally identical to a bullish fair value gap where price only delivered buy-side movement.
glossary.SIBI: Sell-side imbalance, buy-side inefficiency; functionally identical to a bearish fair value gap where price only delivered sell-side movement.
glossary.LIQUIDITY_VOID: A complete gap in the market where neither buy-side nor sell-side liquidity was delivered at all, skipping price ticks entirely.
glossary.VOLUME_IMBALANCE: A two-candle formation where a price gap exists strictly between the close of the first candle and the open of the second candle, while wicks may overlap.
glossary.BPR: Balanced price range; defined by the presenter strictly as the overlapping portion of a bullish FVG and a bearish FVG, without Traidle's 10-candle constraint.
glossary.FVG_SIZE_INDEPENDENCE: The presenter explicitly states there is no premise for how large an FVG must be; any gap between wicks with a candle body qualifies, diverging from Traidle's 1.5x displacement rule.

custom_signals.name: liquidity_void
custom_signals.plain_definition: A complete gap in price delivery where no trading occurred on either the buy or sell side, skipping price ticks entirely.
custom_signals.numeric_definition: open_t > high_{t-1} (bullish void) or open_t < low_{t-1} (bearish void) where gap = [high_{t-1}, open_t] or [open_t, low_{t-1}]

custom_signals.name: volume_imbalance
custom_signals.plain_definition: A two-candle formation where a price gap exists strictly between the close of candle 1 and the open of candle 2, while wicks may overlap.
custom_signals.numeric_definition: candle_{t-1}.close != candle_t.open with body gap between min(candle_{t-1}.close, candle_t.open) and max(candle_{t-1}.close, candle_t.open) while candle_{t-1}.range and candle_t.range wicks overlap

custom_signals.name: bpr_overlap_zone
custom_signals.plain_definition: The exact overlapping price range shared by a bullish fair value gap (BISI) and a bearish fair value gap (SIBI).
custom_signals.numeric_definition: range = [max(fvg_bullish.gap_low, fvg_bearish.gap_low), min(fvg_bullish.gap_high, fvg_bearish.gap_high)] where max(...) < min(...)

custom_signals.name: fvg_without_displacement
custom_signals.plain_definition: A 3-candle fair value gap where any gap exists between wick 1 and wick 3, regardless of candle size or displacement ratio.
custom_signals.numeric_definition: C1.high < C3.low (bullish) or C1.low > C3.high (bearish), without requiring body >= 1.5x rolling average body

sequence: Identify a market inefficiency or imbalance: Fair Value Gap (BISI/SIBI), Balanced Price Range (BPR), Liquidity Void, or Volume Imbalance [00:57, 10:23].

Ensure the imbalance is formed by valid candle geometry: 3 candles for an FVG (gap between wick 1 and wick 3), overlapping opposite FVGs for a BPR, a full price delivery gap for a Liquidity Void, or a 2-candle gap between candle 1 close and candle 2 open for a Volume Imbalance [01:51, 06:06, 07:41, 09:11].

Check for confluence: verify if the imbalance overlaps with another previously established PD array (e.g., order block, breaker block, mitigation block) to form a high-probability Point of Interest [10:34].
Wait for price to navigate towards and rebalance the inefficient price action, noting that price only needs to sting into the imbalance rather than fill it completely [03:14, 08:26].
Anticipate a reaction or continuation once the imbalance has been sufficiently delivered or rebalanced [03:21, 08:30].

invalidation.text: If wicks of candle 1 and candle 3 overlap during formation, no gap exists and the fair value gap is invalid.
A full close through and beyond the imbalance without rejection invalidates the PD array Point of Interest.

filters.text: Do not treat three candles as an FVG if the first wick and third wick overlap, leaving no body space in between.
Imbalances are strongest when overlapping with another PD array; standalone low-timeframe imbalances without context or overlap are prone to failure.

entry_rule.text: Enter when price trades into ('stings into') the imbalance (FVG, BPR overlap zone, Liquidity Void, or Volume Imbalance), particularly when overlapping with another PD array.
entry_rule.quote: it can already sting into it and then just go lower it doesn't have to rebalance it fully

target_rule.text: No specific target rule stated in this episode; imbalances are used as points of interest and rebalancing areas.
target_rule.quote: price is constantly navigating towards those fair value gaps

stop_rule.text: No specific stop loss placement rule is stated in this episode.

management.notes: No trade management rules (breakeven, partials, trailing) are discussed in this conceptual video.

presenter_claims.claim: Price has a very strong tendency—even stronger than a fair value gap—to trade back into a liquidity void before continuing.
There is no premise to how big a fair value gap should be; even the smallest gap between wicks with a little body is a valid fair value gap.
All four imbalance types are strongest when overlapping with another PD array.

strategy_definition.notes: This video functions as a foundational conceptual masterclass on imbalances and gaps rather than a mechanical entry-to-exit strategy guide. The presenter establishes that BISI/SIBI are the technical terms for bullish/bearish FVGs, defines BPR strictly as the overlapping zone between opposing FVGs, and introduces Liquidity Voids and Volume Imbalances as distinct PD arrays.

annotations_drawn_by_presenter.meaning: Highlights the empty space (the body of the middle candle) between the first candle's wick and the third candle's wick.

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: Presenter identifies a three-candle sequence where the first candle's wick and the third candle's wick do not overlap, leaving a gap on the body of the expansive second candle.
Presenter shows an invalid example where a candle has a body, but the preceding and following wicks overlap, leaving no actual gap.
Price later retraces to 'sting into' a valid fair value gap to rebalance the inefficiency without needing to fill it entirely before moving away.

chart_examples.presenter_commentary: He strictly defines the structural geometry of a Fair Value Gap (3 candles, gap between wick 1 and wick 3) and emphasizes that size does not matter. He specifically demonstrates how an overlapping wick invalidates the gap entirely.

may_differ.reason: Traidle requires the displacement candle's body to be >= 1.5x the rolling average. The presenter explicitly states that 'there is no premise to how big a fair value gap should be' and accepts any gap.

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: Presenter highlights an upward displacement gap, defining it as a Buy-Side Imbalance Sell-Side Inefficiency (BISI), equating it directly to a bullish FVG.
Presenter highlights a downward displacement gap, defining it as a Sell-Side Imbalance Buy-Side Inefficiency (SIBI), equating it directly to a bearish FVG.
Price later returns to deliver the missing 'inefficient' price action, fulfilling the sell-side into the BISI or buy-side into the SIBI.

chart_examples.presenter_commentary: The presenter is purely focused on nomenclature here, clarifying that 'BISI' and 'SIBI' are simply the formal institutional terms for bullish and bearish fair value gaps. He notes that if buy-side delivery creates the imbalance, sell-side delivery is subsequently required to fulfill it.
